cases.reviewerAnswer: Cuál identifies a singular referent or information value; cuáles identifies plural referents. Qué before a noun is the usual contemporary Peninsular model.
cases.element: content.body.scope.noteUk: "В Іспанії cuál не ставлять безпосередньо перед іменником: ¿Qué libro?, а не «¿Cuál libro?»."
cases.defect: The categorical geographical prohibition overstates the distinction. Adnominal interrogative cuál exists; its use is substantially more frequent in America than in Spain. A regional preference should not be presented as an exceptionless prohibition.
cases.correction: State that qué before a noun is the usual contemporary Peninsular pattern, while adnominal cuál is much more frequent in American Spanish.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, entry «cuál», interrogative adjectival use before a noun and geographical distribution (from memory).
cases.notes: The supplied examples with qué and pronominal cuál/cuáles are correct.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Extract the requested factual detail from each notice.
Give a short Spanish sentence or an appropriate answer fragment containing the requested information.
Aviso: masculine noun; plural avisos; notice or message.
Dirección: feminine noun; plural direcciones; address or direction.
Entrada: feminine noun; plural entradas; entrance or admission ticket.
Farmacia de guardia: pharmacy on duty.
Sala: feminine noun; plural salas; room or hall.
Salida: feminine noun; plural salidas; exit or departure.
Vacaciones: feminine plural noun in the intended ordinary usage; holiday, leave or school holidays.
